areas.name: Household choices
areas.track: Spending by category on both sides; trip purpose and frequency; travel time and cost; access to better-value or otherwise unavailable goods and services.
areas.records: Existing travel and expenditure surveys, complemented where suitable by aggregated payment data.
areas.decision: Distinguish household gains, movable spending and travel burdens.
areas.limit: Keep samples consistent and account for cash and platform coverage. Records are not assumed accessible or linkable.

areas.name: Business adjustment
areas.track: Sales, transactions, staffing, recorded costs and continued operation; changes in products, customers or operating model, separated by sector, location, employment size and ownership.
areas.records: A consistent business sample using suitable surveys, licensing or business records, recording exits, relocations and operator changes.
areas.decision: Distinguish demand shifts from costs or other constraints and identify where adjustment support may help.
areas.limit: Surviving firms alone can give a misleading picture. Dissolution, outlet closure, relocation and payment-provider changes are different events; employment size does not identify chain ownership.

areas.name: Worker transitions
areas.track: Time to the next job; destination occupation and industry; monthly and hourly earnings; hours; status at six and twelve months, including self-employment, training and labour-force exit.
areas.records: Employment-service and administrative records, with targeted follow-up for missing groups and non-participants or non-completers where feasible.
areas.decision: Identify workable transitions and groups needing different support.
areas.limit: Keep earnings, hours and destinations distinct. Retirement, care, training and self-employment are not automatically failed transitions; report coverage, non-response and attrition.

areas.name: Access to growth
areas.track: Registration followed by paid professional work; supplier introductions, qualification, paid contracts and repeat business; residents hired and retained in growing activities.
areas.records: Relevant registration, procurement, employer and programme records where feasible, including contract value and sustained work when useful.
areas.decision: Distinguish formal access and activity counts from actual earning opportunities.
areas.limit: Registration, introductions and supplier qualification do not by themselves establish contracts, earnings or causal programme gains.

areas.name: Everyday services
areas.track: Jobs or moves delayed or forgone because of housing, care, schooling or healthcare; relevant costs, eligibility, waiting times and completed service hand-offs.
areas.records: A few targeted questions in existing applications, onboarding or follow-up for users with a relevant need.
areas.decision: Identify the practical arrangement on which a specific job or move depends and prioritise economically consequential barriers.
areas.limit: Do not assume every service is equally important or that a reported barrier establishes routine system failure.

areas.name: Useful connections
areas.track: Knowing where to seek help; whether a referral or introduction produced useful information, practical help, a customer or work opportunity; who remains unreached.
areas.records: Short voluntary questions in existing follow-up about whether help was received and used.
areas.decision: Assess reach and useful assistance rather than attendance or contact counts.
areas.limit: A contact does not establish received help, and a referral does not establish resolution. Do not assign a GDP value to friendships.

areas.name: Established residents
areas.track: Housing costs relative to income, relevant service access, local employment and supplier participation, distinguishing established residents and newcomers where feasible.
areas.records: Selected local household, housing, service and employment series with residence defined at the chosen reference point.
areas.decision: Examine access to new opportunities alongside possible cost pressures for existing residents.
areas.limit: Residence is not the same as citizenship. State definitions of existing residents and local suppliers, and do not assume observed pressures were caused by integration.

areas.name: Institutions and reliability
areas.track: Resolution time, repeated hand-offs, cases outside provider remits and user-confirmed resolution; missed work and interrupted essential services during actual disruptions.
areas.records: Existing case records with common categories and aggregated reporting, supported by user confirmation where relevant.
areas.decision: Identify a specific coordination issue, the responsible provider and consequences of unreliable access.
areas.limit: A closed ticket is not necessarily a resolved problem. Do not infer disruption effects from ordinary service activity alone.

regions.name: Singapore–Johor
regions.approach: Use historical series and a reference point before RTS passenger service opens for selected businesses, households and services. Follow outcomes at suitable intervals, including Johor residents and suppliers as well as Singapore households and firms.
regions.caveat: This is a pre-RTS reference point, not a baseline before integration in general. Account for seasonality, anticipation and other changes; distinguish RTS from the JS-SEZ agreement, investment projects and workforce programmes.

regions.name: Hong Kong–Shenzhen
regions.approach: Follow particular business activities, workers, registration-to-work pathways or service referrals over time, starting with existing establishment, employment, vacancy and programme data.
regions.caveat: A credible general pre-integration baseline is unavailable. Comparisons need similar groups with different exposure and checks on other influences; Hong Kong and Shenzhen are not simply each other’s unaffected control.

principles: This is a selective menu for responsible agencies, associations, employers and service providers, not a new resilience index, a requirement to measure everything or additional primary fellowship research.
Check existing fields, coverage and reporting first. Use available records and fill selected gaps only when the information would change a decision; access and linkage are not assumed.

Match effort to the decision: routine monitoring of reach, relevant outcomes and cost; proportionate follow-up; and credible comparison-based evaluation for substantial or expanding interventions. Before-and-after improvement alone is not causal evidence.

Select one main outcome and a few diagnostic measures per intervention: net savings and reliability for shared purchasing; additional and repeat transactions for promotion; sustained work, pay and hours for career conversion; useful assistance for referrals.
Track household benefits alongside business and worker pressures. Follow the same firms or people where feasible, include exits and non-completers, and show denominators, non-response and attrition.

Use proportionate secure access and aggregated publication. A bilateral comparison need not transfer identifiable records across the border; agree useful definitions and periods while retaining appropriate local data custody.

Assign follow-up to existing responsible organisations and use bilateral coordination only where action is required on both sides. Public support should meet demonstrated needs with benefits that justify its cost.

Existing practices are starting points, not proof of this proposed menu: MOM tracks resident re-employment with coverage limits; Skills4Johor requires six-month outcome assessment; DOSM’s 2025 survey covers Malaysian residents’ spending abroad, not Singapore residents’ spending in Johor.
